about: Regional GFS cold starts select the validated aerosol profile through recipe_rules. Other requests retain the native MPAS suite by mesh. Explicit physics requests take precedence, including exact mode. Recipe predicates match all listed context fields; first match wins.

rules.why: MPAS-A v8.4 user's guide (Physics Suites): convection_permitting is the recommended suite where convection-permitting cells (dx < 10 km) are used, including variable-resolution meshes spanning hydrostatic to nonhydrostatic scales; mesoscale_reference is not appropriate at convective scales (New Tiedtke suppresses instability before resolved cells respond). Regions, zoom globes, storm-following members and every variable-resolution mesh with a fine core land here.

Quasi-uniform meshes of 10 km and coarser. MPAS-A's Registry default for them is mesoscale_reference (tested above 10 km), and convection_permitting is also MPAS-A practice there: the guide says it was tested from several hundred kilometres down to 3 km, its Grell-Freitas scheme being scale-aware. hex takes convection_permitting because it is the suite proven bitwise to native MPAS-A over a whole forecast (hl-3) and within 1.2x of the ArWen route on every shape, and on 2025-05-19 it showed no wet bias where the ArWen route was about 2x too wet. mesoscale_reference also runs on the GPU with no native library (24 h strict, every word equal to native MPAS-A v8.4.2) but steps at about 3.3x convection_permitting's cost; switching coarse meshes to it is this row, and waits for it to meet the 1.2x speed bar and for obs skill to favour it.

recipe_rules.why: Three regional GFS cases: FSS improved 27/27, CSI 8/9, area error 7/9; corrected cloud merge and aerosol Thompson, native MYNN settings. No global or cycled-land promotion.
